public_rationale: Vance offered European regulatory examples rather than a demonstrated burden from US AI rules. That does not establish Marcus's stronger assertion that he had no evidence whatsoever. The legal record also shows why having no broad federal AI statute is different from having almost no regulation affecting AI. The available records do not settle the compound claim under its wording.
limitations: Evidence of regulatory existence alone cannot establish excessive regulation.
A missing citation is not proof that evidence did not exist.
The legal examples provide context, not a complete target-date inventory.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Vance has no evidence whatsoever that the US has excessive regulation around AI, and arguably the US has almost no AI regulation at all.

statement.excerpt: What Vance doesn’t have is any evidence whatsoever that the US has excessive regulation around AI; arguably, in fact, it has almost none at all.
statement.document_title: Everything I warned about in Taming Silicon Valley is rapidly becoming our reality

from_speaker: the US has excessive regulation around AI
our_interpretation: Assess the regulatory position and evidence available on February 11, 2025, the date of the remarks and post.
The ordinary reading concerns US regulation affecting AI, including binding sectoral and state rules; it is not limited to a comprehensive federal AI statute.
Treat 'arguably' as qualifying the scarcity assertion.
Failure to cite evidence in a speech does not establish that Vance possessed no evidence whatsoever.
Evidence that regulation exists does not, without evidence of its burdens and benefits, establish that it is excessive.
criteria.support_condition: A sufficiently complete record supports the absence of a credible US-specific evidentiary basis for Vance's position and shows that binding regulation affecting AI was exceptionally limited.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A documented US-specific evidentiary basis available to Vance supports the claimed excessive burden, or a sufficiently complete inventory undermines the assertion of almost no regulation.
